newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leaders of the coalition government meet today to discuss the nomination of Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's successor, amid Banharn's attempts to endorse his party veteran Pramarn Adireksarn rather than Gen Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, leader of the New Aspiration Party. (THE NATION)

- PM Banharn has made changes to the Interior Ministry reshuffle list in what is seen as a bid to leave his stamp on the agency before stepping down. Interior Permanent Secretary says it is up to Banharn, concurrently interior minister, to decide whether to submit the list to the Cabinet today. (BANGKOK POST)
- Thailand has handed over 13 priceless Khmer artifacts to Cambodia, ending six years of acrimony between the two neighbouring countries. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Department of Energy Development and Promotion warned that residents in some northeastern provinces along the Mekong River should be prepared to face big floods this week. The water level has risen as a result of tropical storm Willie and heavy rains are expected to continue through Saturday. (THE NATION)

- Informal survey of 121 local and foreign businessmen and government officials shows Foreign Minister Amnuay Viravan preferred choice to be new prime minister. Majority also say parliament should be dissolved if coalition cannot reach an agreement on who should be new prime minister. (BANGKOK POST)

- State oil officials are resisting efforts by importers seeking to abort a plan to double the amount of oil reserves. Senior government official says yielding to pressure from some companies to keep their reserves at five percent of their trading volume would be unfair to distributors of locally-refined oil products which have been required to keep reserves of 10 percent. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Bank of Thailand has announced the establishment of an eight billion baht fund to support Thailand's maritime sector. The fund will offer loans to private shipping firms looking to purchase vessels. (BANGKOK POST)

- Electricity Generating Plc questioned the merit of plans by its parent, the state-owned Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, to construct new thermal power plants in two southern provinces. (THE NATION)
- Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda says will not take any key decisions before he is replaced in an expected upcoming cabinet reshuffle. (BUSINESS DAY)
